title: VIP Interneurons
intro: Interneurons that express vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) are inhibitory cells whose main job is to inhibit other inhibitory cells. They mostly target SST cells, so when VIP cells fire, the dendrites of pyramidal cells are released from SST inhibition. Because VIP cells are driven by long-range cortical input and by neuromodulators, this disinhibitory circuit is how behavioural state, attention and context reach into a local circuit.

items: Numbers and place: about 10 to 15 per cent of cortical interneurons in mouse, concentrated in layer 2/3, belonging to the 5HT3aR family born in the caudal ganglionic eminence. Many co-express calretinin or cholecystokinin.
Morphology: small, vertically oriented bipolar or bitufted cells, with axons that run vertically across layers within a narrow column.
Firing: irregular spiking or continuous adapting; high input resistance, easily excited.

Inputs: long-range glutamatergic input from other cortical areas (for example motor cortex to barrel cortex, Lee et al. 2013; frontal to visual cortex, Zhang et al. 2014), higher-order thalamus, and neuromodulators: they express ionotropic serotonin (5HT3a) and nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, so serotonin and acetylcholine excite them quickly.
Outputs: mainly SST cells (Pfeffer et al. 2013; Pi et al. 2013), with weaker inhibition of PV cells and only sparse direct inhibition of pyramidal cells.

blocks.source:
context / attention / locomotion / reward
          │  (long-range glutamate, ACh, 5-HT)
          ▼
         VIP ──┤ SST ──┤ pyramidal dendrite

  VIP active   → SST silenced → dendrites released → larger responses
  VIP silent   → SST active   → dendritic input suppressed

  ──┤ = inhibitory connection

blocks.text: Fu et al. (2014) showed this motif at work in mouse V1: locomotion activates VIP cells through cholinergic input from the basal forebrain, VIP cells suppress SST cells, and visual responses of pyramidal cells increase. Pi et al. (2013) found that VIP cells in auditory and prefrontal cortex are recruited by reinforcement signals (reward and punishment), linking disinhibition to learning. Disinhibition is now regarded as a general cortical mechanism for gain control and for gating plasticity (Letzkus, Wolff & Luthi 2015).

items: Single-cell: no famous dedicated VIP model; point models with irregular or adapting spiking are used (Izhikevich regular-spiking or LTS-like parameters, or Allen GLIF fits to Vip cells). Blue Brain's bipolar (BP) and double bouquet (DBC) m-types correspond partly to VIP cells.

Circuit models: Litwin-Kumar, Rosenbaum and Doiron (2016) and Garcia del Molino et al. (2017) showed that in an inhibition-stabilised network the effect of driving VIP cells depends on the strength of recurrent excitation: the same top-down input can raise pyramidal activity at low contrast and lower it at high contrast, matching experiments in mouse V1.
Yang, Murray and Wang (2016) used VIP-SST disinhibition on specific dendritic branches to gate which input pathway reaches the soma.

Predictive-coding circuit models assign VIP cells a role in comparing top-down predictions with bottom-up input: Keller and Mrsic-Flogel (2018) proposed such a circuit for mismatch (prediction-error) neurons in layer 2/3, and Hertag and Sprekeler (2020) showed that a PV-SST-VIP model can learn to produce them.
Rate models of the full PV-SST-VIP triad are common, because each population's role is captured well by its connectivity alone.

blocks.text: What this means for your SNN

items: If your column has an attention, context or reward signal, route it to a VIP-like population rather than directly to excitatory cells.
Wire VIP → SST strongly, VIP → PV weakly, and almost no VIP → pyramidal.
The result is a multiplicative-looking gain on dendritic input without changing feedforward weights, and a gate for plasticity: learning can be allowed only when VIP is active.
In a predictive column, VIP-SST circuits are a candidate mechanism for computing prediction errors between top-down and bottom-up signals.
